summary: Baileys fork aliases libsignal dependency to third-party package at mutable 'latest' tag
details: package.json declares the dependency `libsignal` as an npm alias to `@bellaxchuu/libsignal-node@latest`, a different publisher's package pinned to the mutable `latest` dist-tag with no version constraint and no integrity hash. On `npm install`, resolution fetches whatever that alias currently points to, and the aliased package becomes a transitive code-execution dependency of this package (loaded at require time by the Baileys crypto path). The alias publisher does not match the package author, and the aliased name is unrelated to the upstream libsignal implementations commonly used by Baileys forks. This is an off-registry-style supply-chain redirection: control over the installed libsignal bytes is handed to a third party at every install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
